name: MathlibAnnex.Plucker.derivativeAverage_comp_linear_radial
title: A common orientation sign for the radial derivative average

content.display_title: A common orientation sign for the radial derivative average
content.one_sentence_role: Identifies the whole minor vector using one signed Jacobian integral.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $m,N\in\mathbb N_0$, put $n=m+1>0$, and give $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ their coordinate sup norms. Let $\lambda_n$ be the fixed coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. Let $p,q:E\to\mathbb R$ be continuous real seminorms with specified positive constants $a_p,b_p,a_q,b_q$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty\quad(x\in E).$$

Both $p$ and $q$ are norms. For each $s\in\{p,q\}$ define the closed unit ball, unit sphere, and real reference volume by
$$K_s=\{x:s(x)\le1\},\qquad\Sigma_s=\{x:s(x)=1\},\qquad v_s=\lambda_n(K_s)\in(0,\infty).$$
The finite measure is read as a real number when used as a scalar. Also put $U_p=\{x:p(x)<1\}$ and $U_q=\{x:q(x)<1\}$.

Let $\mathcal I_{n,N}$ be the finite set of increasing $n$-tuples of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. The minor-coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_{n,N}}$ carries its sup norm. For a linear map $B:E\to F$, put $B_{ij}=(Be_j)_i$ in the standard coordinate basis. Write $\Pi_n(B)$ for its maximal-minor vector and $\mathcal V_p(B),\mathcal V_q(B)$ for its two volume-scaled versions. Their coordinates and scaling are
$$\Pi_n(B)_I=\det(B_{i_a,j})_{a,j=1}^n,\qquad\mathcal V_s(B)=v_s\Pi_n(B)\ (s\in\{p,q\})\quad(I=(i_1<\cdots<i_n)).$$

Let $\Delta:\Sigma_p\to\Sigma_q$ be a bijection preserving chord distances, so
$$q(\Delta(u)-\Delta(v))=p(u-v)\qquad(u,v\in\Sigma_p).$$
Read its radial extension on the reference coordinates:
$$R_\Delta(0)=0,\qquad R_\Delta(x)=p(x)\Delta(x/p(x))\quad(x\ne0).$$
For $x\ne0$, positivity of $p(x)$ makes $x/p(x)\in\Sigma_p$, so this is defined.

Let $A:E\to F$ be any linear map and put $H=A\circ R_\Delta$. For a function $k:E\to F$, write $Dk(x)$ for its Fréchet derivative where it exists and for the zero linear map otherwise. Define $G_{p,k}(x)=v_p\Pi_n(Dk(x))$ and $\mathcal A_p(k)=v_p^{-1}\int_{K_p}G_{p,k}\,d\lambda_n$. Then there is one sign $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$ such that
$$\mathcal A_p(A\circ R_\Delta)=\sigma\,\mathcal V_q(A).$$
content.assumptions: The dimension is positive: $n=m+1$. Both $p$ and $q$ are continuous seminorms with the displayed positive norm comparisons. The sphere map is a bijective chord-distance isometry. The map $A$ is arbitrary linear; there is no contraction assumption on it. The output dimension $N$ may be zero.
content.conclusion: One scalar sign works for the full vector, including all selected minors. If $N<n$, the vector identity is in the one-element empty-coordinate space; the same scalar construction still applies.
content.proof_summary: Use signed orientation on open balls, compute linear-composition minors, and cancel the average normalization.

proof_steps.text:
**Supply the signed-Jacobian inputs.** Use the same radial map $R_\Delta$ and its inverse $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$. The radial norm and inverse identities give
$$q(R_\Delta x)=p(x),\qquad R_{\Delta^{-1}}(R_\Delta x)=x,\qquad R_\Delta(R_{\Delta^{-1}}y)=y.$$
The global reference-norm bounds are
$$\frac{a_p}{3b_q}\|x-y\|_\infty\le\|R_\Delta x-R_\Delta y\|_\infty\le\frac{3b_p}{a_q}\|x-y\|_\infty,$$
$$\|R_{\Delta^{-1}}u-R_{\Delta^{-1}}v\|_\infty\le\frac{3b_q}{a_p}\|u-v\|_\infty.$$
These follow from the $3$-Lipschitz radial estimate in the model norms and the positive comparison bounds. The same identities map $U_p$ onto $U_q$, with inverse $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$. Both sets are open; $U_q$ is convex and contains zero, hence is preconnected and has positive measure. Also $U_q\subseteq K_q$, so its measure is finite. [The exact radial input construction](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RadialAverage.lean#L300-L320) records these inputs.

Write $DR_\Delta(x)$ for the derivative of $R_\Delta$ where it exists and for zero otherwise, and set $J_\Delta(x)=\det DR_\Delta(x)$. Apply [the signed Jacobian integral theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Constancy.lean#L72-L97) with source $U_p$, target $U_q$, forward map $R_\Delta$, inverse $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$, and the bounds just displayed. It supplies one sign $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$ and
$$\int_{U_p}J_\Delta(x)\,d\lambda_n(x)=\sigma\,\lambda_n(U_q)=\sigma v_q.$$
For the last equality, the relevant boundary and measure identities are
$$K_q\setminus U_q=\Sigma_q=\partial U_q,\qquad\lambda_n(\Sigma_q)=0,\qquad\lambda_n(U_q)=v_q.$$
[The null-sphere lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RadialAverage.lean#L212-L221) identifies the sphere with the boundary of the convex open ball and proves that it is null. [The open/closed ball-volume identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RadialAverage.lean#L277-L297) gives the last equality. No absolute determinant is substituted.

**Compute every minor with the same inner determinant.** At a differentiability point of $R_\Delta$,
$$DH(x)=A\,DR_\Delta(x),\qquad\Pi_n(DH(x))_I=\Pi_n(A)_I\,J_\Delta(x).$$
Selecting rows commutes with multiplication by the square matrix $DR_\Delta(x)$; determinant multiplicativity then proves the second equality. [The exact linear-composition identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RadialAverage.lean#L176-L194) gives
$$G_{p,H}(x)_I=v_p\Pi_n(A)_I J_\Delta(x).$$ The global Lipschitz bound on $R_\Delta$ gives differentiability almost everywhere. The linear map $A$ is Lipschitz, so $H$ is Lipschitz. [Compact-set integrability of derivative generators](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/Average.lean#L83-L114) applied to $H$ on $K_p$ makes the vector $G_{p,H}$ integrable. Apply the same result to $R_\Delta:E\to E$ on $K_p$, and let $I_0=(1,\ldots,n)$ be the all-row index. Its determinant coordinate gives
$$G_{p,R_\Delta}(x)_{I_0}=v_pJ_\Delta(x),\qquad J_\Delta=v_p^{-1}(G_{p,R_\Delta})_{I_0}\in L^1(K_p,\lambda_n).$$
Coordinate projection and multiplication by the finite constant $v_p^{-1}$ preserve integrability. Thus both the scalar integral and the vector coordinates used below are justified.

**Cancel the normalization and insert the one sign.** For every $I\in\mathcal I_{n,N}$,
$$\begin{aligned}(\mathcal A_p(H))_I&=v_p^{-1}\int_{K_p}v_p\Pi_n(A)_I J_\Delta\,d\lambda_n\\&=\Pi_n(A)_I\int_{K_p}J_\Delta\,d\lambda_n\\&=\Pi_n(A)_I\int_{U_p}J_\Delta\,d\lambda_n\\&=\sigma v_q\Pi_n(A)_I.\end{aligned}$$
The first two equalities use integrability and $v_p>0$. The third discards exactly $K_p\setminus U_p=\Sigma_p$, whose measure is zero by [The null-sphere lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RadialAverage.lean#L212-L221). [The coordinate radial-average theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RadialAverage.lean#L238-L275) records those first three lines; the last substitutes the signed integral from Step 1. The sign was chosen before any row index, so it is common to every coordinate. Reassembling the vector gives $\mathcal A_p(H)=\sigma\mathcal V_q(A)$.

content.lean_realization_notes: The derivative and every integral use the fixed sup-norm coordinates and reference Lebesgue measure. The sign is not chosen independently for individual minors.
